content_preview.title: MCP Working Group Publishes an Experimental Draft for Moving Files Between Clients and Tools Outside Model Context; No Reference Implementation Yet
content_preview.summary: An experimental MCP extension draft, io.modelcontextprotocol/files, would let clients upload and download files for tools out of band; the blog expects it stable by year-end and no reference implementation exists yet.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) project has published an experimental draft for moving files between clients and tools. A [post on the MCP blog](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/exploring-file-uploads-and-downloads-in-mcp/), dated November 10, 2026 (09:00 UTC in the page's metadata), introduces an extension identified as `io.modelcontextprotocol/files` that works with protocol revision 2026-07-28 and later. The post calls the work \"still very much an experimental effort\...

editor_notes.source_verification: Anthropic disclosure: not required by the strict rule (MCP is presented by its own blog footer as 'a Series of LF Projects, LLC' and by The New Stack as part of the Agentic AI Foundation, so it is not an Anthropic-owned or -operated product; Anthropic is not in the headline, summary or lead, and no credit line appears), but the article voluntarily carries the one-sentence disclosure ('The Herald's contributor model is built by Anthropic.') in the closing section, neutrally worded; everything else about Anthropic is attributed to The New Stack. Verified against raw text, not the article: The New Stack feed text says 'Den Delimarsky, lead maintainer of MCP and member of technical staff at Anthropic', 'Anthropic launched the project some two years ago' and a File Uploads Working Group 'initially made up of members from Anthropic and OpenAI'; the MCP blog byline lists Delimarsky as 'Lead Maintainer' (no employer), the draft lists @localden as a contributor, and nothing in the repo contradicts the attribution. SNAPSHOTS READ (gunzip, sha256 matched the manifest): source-1 blog.modelcontextprotocol.io post (page metadata published_time 2026-11-10T09:00:00Z; the post names the 'File Uploads Working Group'; says 'still very much an experimental effort', 'there's no reference implementation yet', 'We expect to finalize the extension and have it become stable before the end of the year'; quotes 'a matching digest confirms that the bytes match the supplied hash, not that the file is safe' and 'they don’t by themselves control where the file goes' verbatim; all attributed blog statements confirmed). source-2 draft spec (embedded commit 8a859b8f2689...; Status: Draft; Working Group: File Uploads; 'Anything here can change before then'; seven numbered Open Questions recounted: Finalize, Tools behind an executor, Resources, omit binding, Failure signal, Download shape, Integrity = 7; 'The group needs to answer this before the extension leaves the experimental phase' and 'The working group has discussed downloads but has not reviewed this shape' verbatim; inline/maxInlineBytes/upload rules, server confirmation before running the tool, host MUST NOT place any target or file bytes in model context, credentials include/omit rules and no-redirect rule all confirmed). Reporters' handles are not named in the article (confirmed). source-9 SEP-1306 is an issue (not a PR) titled 'SEP-1306: Binary Mode Elicitation for File Uploads', opened 2025-08-05T23:36:33Z, closed 2026-03-12T11:37:41Z by localden with the comment 'Superseded by #2356'; source-10 SEP-2356 PR opened 2026-03-05T16:04:40Z, closed unmerged 2026-06-26T17:17:52Z with 'Closing in favor of #2631 which will likely be the more durable solution.'; source-11 SEP-2631 PR opened 2026-04-22T21:05:21Z, closed unmerged 2026-10-14T06:31:35Z with a comment closing it 'in favor of the extension'. Judged sufficient for a News item whose subject is a project's own draft and whose headline claims all rest on the project's own documents, with independent corroboration of the key facts (experimental, no reference implementation, stable targeted for year-end); the article says plainly that only one cited source is independent.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Claim-accuracy tests run (quantifier/absence scan of title, summary and body; every hit tested against all snapshots). Absence claims: 'Neither the blog, the draft, the README nor The New Stack gives a date for a reference implementation' holds (the only date is the blog's 'stable before the end of the year'); 'neither the blog nor the draft names clients or servers that plan to support it' holds (contributor handles and acknowledgments name no supporting implementers); 'not stated in the sources' on adoption of the four suggestions holds (zero comments, no commits after 8a859b8). Quantifiers: 'three earlier proposals, all now closed; the two pull requests among them were not merged' holds (1306 is an issue); 'seven items' recounted = 7; 'four open issues, all opened on November 12 and none with a comment' holds. Dates: all UTC and recomputed from the API; blog date and 09:00 UTC from page metadata. Headline tests: 'Experimental Draft' (README 'experimental extension', spec 'Status: Draft', blog 'experimental effort'); 'for Moving Files Between Clients and Tools Outside Model Context' matches README and spec abstract; 'No Reference Implementation Yet' matches blog, README ('will live in this repository'), spec ('will include'), The New Stack, and the empty repo tree; it is a statement as of 13 November. Two imprecisions, both clarifications and not errors in the lead: (1) the headline calls the publisher 'MCP Working Group' whereas every source names it the 'File Uploads Working Group' (the README says it maintains the repository; the blog says it 'bootstrapped' it), and the article body never names it (the lead says 'the Model Context Protocol (MCP) project'); (2) the summary says the extension would let clients upload and download files 'out of band', but the draft also allows small uploads inline (the body covers this correctly). Neither makes the headline or summary false, so no REJECT.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, attributive and hedged; the Herald's own readings (proposal dates and states, seven-question count, issue check) are labelled as the Herald's; no AI self-reference beyond the policy disclosure; no characterisation of Anthropic or MCP beyond what The New Stack states.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No existing article covers the MCP file-transfer extension; the recent MCP articles in the archive (TypeScript SDK 2.3.0, Glow Labs MCP-server selection) cover other stories. No open PR duplicates it.
concerns: Headline names the body 'MCP Working Group'; the sources call it the File Uploads Working Group, and the article body never names it (clarification filed).
Summary says 'out of band' for uploads and downloads while the draft also permits inline uploads for small files (clarification filed).

Sourcing is mostly first-party (11 of 12 sources are the project's own records); The New Stack is the single independent outlet and its page was only readable through its RSS feed and a reader-proxy copy, not through the stored snapshot.
recommendations: Name the specific working group (File Uploads Working Group) in the headline or lead when the sources do.
Where a summary compresses a flow with alternatives (inline or out of band), keep both alternatives.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully scoped and well hedged coverage of an experimental draft; every headline element (experimental, draft, scope, no reference implementation yet) is supported by the project's own documents and corroborated by The New Stack, and the GitHub readings were re-verified at read time. Approved with two clarification-level corrections (publisher named loosely in the headline; summary omits the inline option). Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate, well-scoped coverage of an early experimental MCP draft for a defined audience of protocol implementers and agent-tool developers
